_comment: Control groups can nest (hierarchically): binding a selection that's exactly the combined membership of one or more OTHER already-bound groups -- no partial overlap, no extra units -- records the new group as a COMPOSITE over those groups instead of a flat snapshot, so recalling it always live-resolves to whatever its nested groups currently hold. A drill-mode scenario (no enemy needed -- this is a pure selection/UI mechanic) with four well-separated Infantry units on their own: unit 0 alone becomes group 2; units 1+2 together become group 3; selecting exactly {0, 1, 2} -- the clean union of groups 2 and 3, with no leftovers -- and Ctrl+1 records group 1 as nested over groups 2 and 3. Unit 3 is a control unit that's never grouped or recalled. The selection is then deliberately switched to unit 3 (so the next step can't be mistaken for a no-op), and pressing 1 alone recalls group 1, live-reselecting exactly units 0/1/2. A move order issued right after moves only those three -- unit 3 stays put -- proving the recall (and the order it carries) resolved to the nested union, not to unit 3 or an empty selection. Driven live through the real SelectionManager by tools/demo/DemoInputRecorder.gd; world coordinates; physics ticks (60/s).
